## Context
During A6-1 read-only review-bot drain inspection, the container's HTTP access log printed the full webhook request target, including the bearer credential carried in the query string. The credential value is deliberately omitted here. Anyone with journal access can recover it, and diagnostic tooling can accidentally copy it into other logs.

## Plan
- Change webhook authentication/logging so request logs never contain the credential (prefer a header or a redacted request-target logging seam).
- Add regression coverage that sends a request with a sentinel secret and proves the secret is absent from captured access/application logs while authentication behavior remains fail-closed.
- Rotate the production webhook credential after the redaction fix is deployed, update its configured callers, and verify the prior credential is rejected.
- Assess the bounded journal retention/exposure and document any required log cleanup without reproducing the secret.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] [code-verifiable] A sentinel webhook credential never appears in HTTP access or application logs for accepted or rejected requests.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] Valid webhook authentication still succeeds and missing/invalid authentication remains rejected after the transport/redaction change.
- [ ] [operator-attested] The production credential is rotated after the fix deploys, all legitimate callers use the replacement, and the prior credential is rejected.
- [ ] [operator-attested] The retained journal exposure is assessed and any required cleanup receipt is recorded without copying the credential into the ticket.

## Scope
Review-bot webhook authentication/access logging and focused tests; production secret rotation is an operator deployment step. This bug is discovered from A6-1 but must not expand or block the tickets-history reclaim once the current queue is safely drained.
compiled_state.title: Redact review-bot webhook credential from access logs and rotate it
